basis: Sarcoma arising in the colon; no other organ is consistently affected across subtypes.
Defined by failure of respiratory function in the newborn.
Inherited focal epilepsy; nocturnal seizures occur in 10/10 reported patients.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and digit malformations define BBS; renal abnormalities are a major criterion. Intellectual disability (1/3) omitted by cap.
Tonsillar carcinoma arises in the oropharynx, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Congenital absence or malformation of eyelids with ocular coverage and often microphthalmia; isolated ocular disorder.
Primary antibody deficiency; associated infections and autoimmune diseases are separate diagnoses, and many patients are asymptomatic.
Diabetes and optic atrophy define Wolfram syndrome; deafness is a cardinal feature (60-90%). Hydronephrosis occurs in 80%; common neurologic degeneration omitted by cap.
Inherited surfactant metabolism disorder causing alveolar surfactant accumulation and chronic pulmonary dysfunction.
Central and peripheral neurodegeneration define TECPR2 disease. Central apnea is neurologic; reflux and respiratory infections are separate diagnoses.
Malignant mature B-cell lymphoma; no single extranodal organ is directly affected in at least 30% across the umbrella.
Primary fallopian tube carcinoma; reproductive organs have no axis, and metastatic sites are not inherent labels.
10p13-p14 deletion overlaps DiGeorge 2: developmental impairment, hypoparathyroidism and thymic deficiency; congenital cardiac defects are major diagnostic features.
Facial nerve dysfunction producing unilateral facial spasms; muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle disease.
Defective vitamin D metabolism or action causes hypocalcemia and impaired skeletal mineralization; both axes define the disease.
Branched-chain amino acid catabolic defect; progressive encephalopathy affects most untreated classic cases. Central respiratory failure reflects brain dysfunction.
Occlusive disease of pulmonary veins and capillaries causing pulmonary hypertension and impaired pulmonary gas exchange.
NR4A2-related neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability, language impairment and dystonia-parkinsonism; no established systemic metabolic defect.
Cholesterol emboli occlude renal vessels and directly injure the kidney; both the vascular lesion and renal location define it.
Congenital sensory and cognitive dysfunction; corneal sensory loss with keratitis occurs in 30-79%. Fractures and osteomyelitis are separately diagnosed injury complications.
Allergic immune-mediated inflammation of skin triggered by ingested food; ingestion does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Defined by vascular lesions of the liver, including occlusion, thrombosis and vascular neoplasms.
Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma; skin and lymphoid cell origin define it. Visceral spread is not common across the typically indolent group.
Ischemic brain necrosis in a cerebral arterial territory; visual field loss reflects brain injury rather than direct ocular damage.
Primordial skeletal growth disorder with osteodysplasia, microcephaly and neurodevelopmental impairment; no other organ involvement established.
